It logs each `toLocaleString` call and its output so you can observe both the thousands‐separator insertion and how fractional rounding/leading zeros behave when only maximumFractionDigits or both minimumVariationDigits are set.
1.bug_scenario: The attached console screenshot shows how JavaScript’s Number.prototype.toLocaleString behaves when only `maximumFractionDigits` (and in one case also `minimumFractionDigits`) is specified. Large numbers get the locale’s thousands‐separator (e.g. “2,445”), and fractional values are rounded to the specified maximum fraction digits. Very small fractional parts (like 0.000001) get rounded down to an integer, unless you also specify a minimum fraction digits, and larger fractions (like 0.006) round up correctly.
